paragraphs: Ara Daila [ארא; later אדא], Rav Yehudah’s student. Rav Yehudah was tall in his generation, and Adda Daila reached his shoulder, Niddah 24b; see Abba Shaul. Rashi: daila attends sages; some say a water-drawer. Rav Yehudah blessed over the light in Adda’s house at Shabbat’s departure, although it was far from his own, end of Ellu Devarim 53b. Rabbi Yehudah ruled for him, Bava Kamma 119a. Rashi, Avodah Zarah, end of chapter 2, 40b: an attendant customarily hired by someone holding a feast to prepare the dishes. See Yoma 18a: if your sister’s son is an attendant in the market, do not pass before him.
